title: Registration and Attach · 5G SA / LTE
description: Investigate Aurora's registration rejections after switching profiles between operators; compare 5G SA, the LTE control and the Boreal CDUT.

dut-vantis-zenith.label: Aurora · Vantis → Zenith · 5G SA
dut-vantis-zenith.title: Registration rejection cascade

evidence.title: Attempt 1 · previous operator context
evidence.html: On PCI 177, SIB1 advertises PLMN 724/085. The Registration Request uses SUCI 724/085 and receives 5GMM Cause #3 · Illegal UE.

evidence.title: Attempt 2 · target PLMN, old SUCI
evidence.html: On PCI 201, the selected PLMN is already 724/078, but the SUCI sent still carries Home-Network-Id 724/085. The network rejects with 5GMM Cause #11 · PLMN not allowed.

evidence.title: Attempt 3 · identity aligned
evidence.html: The new Registration Request presents SUCI 724/078; Authentication, Security Mode, Registration Accept and Registration Complete follow.

evidence.title: The failure happens after acquisition and RRC
evidence.html: PSS/SSS, MIB, SIB1 and RRC Setup complete in the rejected attempts. The divergence is in the NAS registration sequence, not in cell detection.

dut-vantis-zenith.notice: The attached log covers the 3 attempts of one of the five switches in scenario 1; the document does not say which. The log duration (4.55 s, from PSS/SSS detection to Registration Complete) matches the time of switch 03. There are no individual logs for the other switches. The exact internal causality of the SUCI transition is not proven by these logs: correlate the profile state and the provisioned identity.
dut-vantis-zenith.logLabel: Source: Desafio_S02_Log_DUT_Aurora.html · scenario 1 · 36 messages / 3 attempts · 4.55 s. Original log, unmodified.

timelineLabels.note: Total time to registration complete, in seconds · bars show the range over the 5 switches

guide.title: After the switch, the old operator's cell
guide.text: The active profile is already Zenith's, but the Aurora first syncs to PCI 177, the Vantis cell. This is T 0: the case measures the total time from here.

guide.title: SIB1 announces Vantis
guide.text: PLMN 724/085 in SIB1. The cell is good (RSRP −80 dBm) and not barred: radio is not the problem.

guide.title: Attempt 1: the old profile's identity
guide.text: Registration Request with SUCI Home-Network-Id 724/085 and MSIN 4185551234, the Vantis identity. Selected PLMN and SUCI match, but both belong to the profile that was just replaced.

guide.title: Rejection #3 · Illegal UE
guide.text: The Vantis AMF refuses the identity presented (5GMM cause #3). Note where the arrow comes from: the core, through the gNodeB. The rejection is NAS, not radio. Under TS 24.501, after #3 the UE shall consider the USIM invalid for 5GS until it is switched off or the card is removed.

guide.title: New search: now the Zenith cell
guide.text: 1.17 s after the release, the UE syncs to PCI 201 (Zenith), the operator of the active profile.

guide.title: Right PLMN: 724/078
guide.text: In RRCSetupComplete the UE already selects PLMN 724/078. So far, the same as the Boreal.

guide.title: Attempt 2: PLMN ≠ SUCI
guide.text: The exact point of divergence. The selected PLMN is Zenith's (724/078), but the SUCI still carries Home-Network-Id 724/085 and the Vantis MSIN (4185551234). See the identity card in red.

guide.title: Rejection #11 · PLMN not allowed
guide.text: The Zenith AMF refuses a subscriber whose home network (724/085) is not its own. The network reacts correctly to the wrong identity. Under the standard, the UE stores the rejected PLMN in the forbidden list and selects again. Going back to Zenith only makes sense because the identity changes; repeating SUCI 724/085 after #3 already shows the Aurora mixing data from the old and the new profile.

guide.title: Attempt 3, on the same cell
guide.text: 1.91 s later, a new RRC connection on PCI 201, with no new cell search. Only what the UE sends will change.

guide.title: Identity finally aligned
guide.text: SUCI with Home-Network-Id 724/078 and MSIN 7729004321, the Zenith profile's identity. Same cell, same network: the only difference from attempt 2 is the identity.

guide.title: The network recognizes the subscriber
guide.text: Authentication Request (RAND/AUTN): the Zenith AMF accepted the identity and starts authentication, followed by Security Mode (NIA2/NEA2).

guide.title: Registered at T +4.55 s
guide.text: Registration Complete on the 3rd attempt, matching the time of switch 03 in the case. The Boreal, on the same cell, registers in 0.82 s on the 1st attempt.

cdut-boreal.label: Boreal · Vantis → Zenith · 5G SA
cdut-boreal.title: Boreal registers on the first attempt
cdut-boreal.description: Boreal · Vantis (724/085) → Zenith (724/078) · same cells as scenario 1

evidence.title: Same site and same cells
evidence.html: The CDUT accesses PCI 201/PLMN 724/078; the network accepts the Registration Request already carrying SUCI 724/078.

evidence.title: Complete NAS sequence
evidence.html: Authentication Request/Response, Security Mode Command/Complete, Registration Accept and Registration Complete.

evidence.title: 5G SA registration at first try
evidence.html: 5/5 switches complete on the first attempt; the detailed log shows a single successful attempt.

evidence.title: The contrast points to the DUT, it does not prove the implementation
evidence.html: DUT and CDUT differ in SIM/identity state and hardware; the control localizes the deviation in Aurora but does not by itself identify the internal mechanism.

guide.title: Straight to the Zenith cell
guide.text: After the same Vantis → Zenith switch, the Boreal syncs straight to PCI 201. It never goes through the old operator's cell. T 0.

guide.title: PLMN 724/078
guide.text: In RRCSetupComplete the selected PLMN is Zenith's, as on the Aurora from attempt 2 onwards.

guide.title: SUCI aligned on the 1st attempt
guide.text: Home-Network-Id 724/078 and MSIN 7729009876: the Zenith profile's identity. This is exactly what the Aurora lacks on attempts 1 and 2.

guide.title: Authentication without rejection
guide.text: The Zenith AMF answers with Authentication Request: no NAS rejection.

guide.title: NAS security
guide.text: Security Mode Command with NIA2/NEA2, the same algorithms as the Aurora's attempt 3.

guide.title: Registered at T +0.82 s
guide.text: Registration Complete on the 1st attempt. The case reports 0.98–1.15 s for scenario 4; the log is shorter because the document does not define when the measurement starts.

rf.title: Coverage / RF
rf.question: Was the Aurora in worse radio conditions than the Boreal?

evidence.text: Good, unbarred cells: Vantis PCI 177 (−80 dBm / −7 dB) and Zenith PCI 201 (−83 dBm / −8 dB), the same ones used by the Boreal.
The rejected attempts complete PSS/SSS, MIB, SIB1 and RRC Setup: the radio link works.
Both rejections are NAS (Registration Reject from the AMF), not RRC or access failures.

rf.verdict: Ruled out: radio and the RRC connection work in every attempt; the refusal comes from the core.

cell.title: Zenith cell or planning
cell.question: Does cell PCI 201 (or its TAC) refuse new subscribers?

evidence.text: The Boreal registers on the first attempt on the same PCI 201 and TAC 0x1042.
The Aurora's own attempt 3 is accepted on the same cell that rejected attempt 2.
On the Zenith → Nimbus switch (PCI 133) the Aurora also needs three attempts (aggregate result, no log).

cell.verdict: Ruled out: the same cell accepts the Boreal and the Aurora itself, and the symptom repeats on another operator.

core.title: Zenith core rejecting wrongly
core.question: Does the Zenith AMF refuse a subscriber it should accept?

evidence.text: In attempt 2 the Aurora presents a SUCI with Home-Network-Id 724/085 (Vantis). #11 "PLMN not allowed" is the correct answer for a subscriber with no agreement with Zenith.
With SUCI 724/078, the same AMF authenticates, activates security and accepts the registration.

core.verdict: Ruled out: the network reacts correctly to the identity it receives. The error is in the identity sent.

band.title: Band or RAT
band.question: Is the problem the n78 band or 5G radio access?

evidence.text: On LTE Band 3, the same Aurora attaches on the first attempt in 5/5 switches (aggregate result).
On n78, the Boreal registers on the first attempt and the Aurora fails with two destination operators.

band.verdict: Ruled out as a band issue: n78 works for the Boreal. The LTE control points to the Aurora's 5GS registration path (identity and SUCI), not the frequency.

provisioning.title: Zenith profile not provisioned yet
provisioning.question: Did the Aurora's new profile not exist in the Zenith UDM yet?

evidence.text: In attempts 1 and 2 the Aurora does not even present the Zenith identity: it sends SUCI 724/085 and MSIN 4185551234.
The first time it presents SUCI 724/078 (MSIN 7729004321), it is authenticated with no rejection.
The Boreal uses another subscription (MSIN 7729009876): its success does not prove the Aurora's profile was provisioned.

provisioning.verdict: Unlikely, but not fully ruled out by the logs: the network never refused the new identity. To close it, check the UDM or repeat with the device powered on already with the Zenith profile.

ue.title: Aurora using old-profile data
ue.question: After the switch, does the Aurora keep using the Vantis profile's PLMN and identity?

evidence.text: Attempt 1: goes back to the Vantis cell (PLMN 724/085) with the Vantis SUCI → #3.
Attempt 2: selects PLMN 724/078 but still sends SUCI 724/085 → #11.
Attempt 3: identity aligned (SUCI 724/078) and registration accepted. The Boreal starts this way.

ue.verdict: Supported: the only mechanism that explains both rejections, their order and the success on the third attempt. It should not be marked as ruled out.

conclusion.title: Most likely mechanism
conclusion.summary: After the profile switch, the Aurora keeps using Vantis profile data in the 5G SA registration. Only on the third attempt does it use the Zenith profile identity. The network answers correctly at every step.
symptoms: Attempt 1: the device goes back to the old operator (Vantis cell and PLMN) with the old SUCI and gets #3 Illegal UE.

Attempt 2: it already selects Zenith, but the SUCI still carries Home-Network-Id 724/085 and the Vantis MSIN, and it gets #11 PLMN not allowed. Under TS 24.501, after #3 the USIM should be treated as invalid for 5GS; repeating the same identity shows the device mixing data from the old and the new profile.
conclusion.closing: The Aurora's own LTE control registers on the first attempt, which points to the 5GS-specific data (SUCI and 5G location stored in the device) not being read again after the eSIM switch, which should make the device read the USIM again.
conclusion.statsTitle: What is missing to close it with statistical certainty
stats: The current result is already significant: 5/5 Aurora switches with rejection × 0/5 for the Boreal gives p ≈ 0.008 (Fisher's exact). More repetitions narrow the confidence interval.
Control without a switch: power on the Aurora already with the Zenith profile. If it registers on the first attempt, the defect is in handling the switch, not in the profile.
Switch followed by airplane mode or a reboot: if registration then succeeds on the first attempt, it supports the cached-data hypothesis.
SIM/eUICC log (APDUs): REFRESH after the profile switch and reads of EF IMSI, EF SUCI_Calc_Info and EF 5GS3GPPLOCI.
Zenith core log (AMF/UDM), to fully rule out a provisioning delay.
NAS capture of the Zenith → Nimbus switch and the Boreal in the same scenario, which today only have aggregate results.
